items.name: Karpathy Skills
items.what: One CLAUDE.md / skill with four rules: think first, simplicity, surgical changes, goal-driven.
items.alt: Per project instead: curl -o CLAUDE.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills/main/CLAUDE.md
items.use: Automatic once installed.

items.name: Matt Pocock Skills
items.what: 27 skills for real engineering, built around one main flow: grill-with-docs (interview you about a plan), to-spec, to-tickets, implement (test-first), code-review and retro, plus grill-me, tdd, diagnosing-bugs, wayfinder and handoff. Catalogue at aihero.dev/skills.
items.alt: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills
items.use: Run /setup-matt-pocock-skills once per repo, then /grill-with-docs → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement → /code-review. Not sure which skill fits? /ask-matt.
items.note: Since v1.3 (October 2026) project vocabulary lives in GLOSSARY.md, not CONTEXT.md: re-run /setup-matt-pocock-skills in repos set up earlier. The Claude app zips here cover the main flow; /ask-matt and setup only make sense in Claude Code.

items.name: ECC (Everything Claude Code)
items.what: Huge harness: 408 skills, 71 agents, hooks, memory, AgentShield security scan.
items.alt: Rule packs are separate: clone the repo and copy rules/common (+ your language) into ~/.claude/rules/.
items.use: /plugin configure ecc@ecc to set hook options.
items.note: Heaviest by far: ~47.6k tokens added to every session. Only download from github.com/affaan-m/ECC or npm ecc-universal.

items.name: Agent Skills (Addy Osmani)
items.what: Senior-engineer lifecycle: /spec, /plan, /build, /test, /review, /code-simplify, /ship.
items.alt: npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills
items.use: /spec then /plan then /build.
items.note: Independent placebo test (skill-placebo, Sep 2026, Opus 5.5, 15 coding tasks): 5% cheaper than a same-length placebo, same pass rate.

items.name: Superpowers
items.what: Brainstorm, write plan, TDD, subagent execution, code review, verification before done.
items.alt: Also in Anthropic's plugin directory: /plugin install superpowers (search 'superpowers' in /plugin).
items.use: Automatic; starts with brainstorming before code.

items.name: Ponytail
items.what: Lazy-senior-dev rules: write the least code that works, mark every shortcut.
items.alt: Cursor/Windsurf/Cline: copy the matching rules file from the repo.
items.use: /ponytail:ponytail ultra, /ponytail:ponytail-review
items.note: The README's numbers are the author's benchmark. An independent placebo test (skill-placebo, Sep 2026, Opus 5.5) found it 12% cheaper than a same-length placebo, but against no skill: about 13% less code and no measurable token saving. Test it on your own tasks.

items.name: Career Ops
items.what: Job-search command center: scores job posts against your CV, tailors ATS PDFs, tracks applications.
items.alt: npx @career-ops-hq/career-ops init
items.use: cd ~/career-ops, add cv.md, run claude, then /career-ops <job URL>.
items.note: Works as a project folder. Draft-only: never submits applications.

items.name: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
items.what: CLI + MCP that lets the agent decompile and explain how an app works without its source.
items.alt: npx -y rea-agents analyze /Applications/Notes.app
items.use: Ask: 'Use REA to explain how search works in the Notes app.'
items.note: Setup targets macOS (installs Homebrew + Hopper). Fake trojan 'REA.exe' copies exist: only use github.com/morluto/rea, rea.tools or npm rea-agents.

items.name: Graphify
items.what: Turns a folder of code, docs, PDFs and images into a queryable knowledge graph.
install: pipx install graphifyy || python3 -m pip install --user graphifyy
items.alt: python3 -m pip install graphifyy && graphify install
items.use: /graphify . in Claude Code, or graphify update <path> (code-only, no LLM).
items.tested: 0.9.95 built; mapped a repo: 958 nodes offline
items.note: PyPI name is graphifyy (double y).

items.name: Understand Anything
items.what: Multi-agent codebase analysis into an interactive graph dashboard, guided tours, diff impact.
items.alt: Other agents: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything/main/install.sh | bash -s codex
items.use: /understand then /understand-dashboard
items.note: First /understand on a big repo burns a lot of tokens; later runs are incremental.

items.name: Last 30 Days
items.what: Researches a topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, GitHub and the web over the last 30 days.
items.alt: git clone https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill.git ~/.claude/skills/last30days
items.use: /last30days <topic>; run /last30days setup to add API keys.
items.note: More sources unlock with keys in ~/.config/last30days/.env. Runs take 2-8 minutes.

items.name: Agent Reach
items.what: One CLI that lets the agent read X, Reddit, YouTube transcripts, GitHub, RSS and more.
items.alt: npx skills add Panniantong/Agent-Reach@agent-reach
items.use: Ask the agent to read a tweet, Reddit thread or YouTube video.
items.note: Many guides still show 'agent-reach install --env=auto'; v1.6 replaced it with 'agent-reach setup'. X/Reddit need a login (agent-reach login <channel>); cookies stay local.

items.name: Headroom
items.what: Compresses tool output, logs, files and history before the model reads them.
install: pipx install headroom-ai || python3 -m pip install --user headroom-ai
items.alt: Full ML compressors (large download): pipx install "headroom-ai[all]". Or skip the plugin and run: headroom wrap claude
items.use: headroom perf to see savings; headroom unwrap claude to undo.
items.note: README itself says 15-20% savings for coding agents (60-95% is for JSON-heavy data).

items.name: BMAD Method
items.what: Agile team of agents: analyst, PM, architect, dev, QA with stories and reviews.
items.alt: Non-interactive: npx bmad-method install --yes --modules bmm --tools claude-code. v7 preview: npx skills add bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD
items.use: Run inside a project folder, then /bmad-help.
items.note: Installs per project (run it in the project folder).

install: mkdir -p ~/bmad-ci && cd ~/bmad-ci && npx -y bmad-method install --yes --directory . --modules bmm --tools claude-code --user-name ci

items.name: Claude-Mem
items.what: Captures what happens in sessions and injects compressed memory into new ones.
items.use: Automatic; search with the mem-search skill.
items.note: Runs a background worker (Bun). Data lives in ~/.claude-mem.

items.name: gstack
items.what: Garry Tan's setup: CEO/eng/design plan reviews, /review, /qa, /ship, /retro and more.
items.use: /office-hours, /plan-ceo-review, /review, /ship
items.tested: v1.91 installed (browser part needs Chromium download)
items.note: Its setup asks you to add CLAUDE.md lines telling Claude to use gstack's /browse instead of Claude in Chrome.

items.name: Caveman
items.what: Makes replies terse caveman-speak; also compresses CLAUDE.md files.
items.use: /caveman, /caveman-compress CLAUDE.md
items.note: An independent placebo test (skill-placebo) found no significant output-token saving and ~14% higher cost on Opus 5.5.

items.name: GSD (Get Shit Done)
items.what: Spec-driven phases with fresh subagent contexts so big builds don't drift.
items.alt: Old package (archived May 2026): npx get-shit-done-cc --claude --global
items.use: /gsd-help, then /gsd-new-project
items.note: gsd-build/get-shit-done moved to open-gsd/gsd-core. gsd-core declares Node 24+ (worked on 22 with a warning).

items.name: Taste
items.what: Anti-template frontend art direction: picks a deliberate visual direction, runs a preflight review.
items.alt: npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill design-taste-frontend
items.use: Automatic on landing pages and redesigns.

items.name: Archify
items.what: Architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow and lifecycle diagrams as one interactive HTML file.
items.alt: Manual: copy the archify/ folder into ~/.claude/skills/
items.use: 'Use archify to draw a high-level architecture of this repo.'

items.name: Diagram Design
items.what: Editorial, on-brand diagrams (40+ types) as HTML/SVG/PNG.
items.alt: npx skills add https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design --skill diagram-design
items.use: Ask for a diagram; it asks for brand tokens first.

items.name: Impeccable
items.what: Design language for agents: 23 commands (critique, polish, audit) and anti-pattern detectors.
items.alt: npx impeccable install
items.use: /impeccable init once, then /impeccable critique <target>

items.name: UI UX Pro Max
items.what: Searchable catalog of UI styles, palettes, font pairings and UX rules across stacks.
items.alt: npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli && uipro init --ai claude --global
items.use: Automatic on UI work.

items.name: PPT Master
items.what: Turns a PDF, DOCX, URL or Markdown into a natively editable PowerPoint (real shapes, not images).
items.use: 'Make a deck from this PDF.'
items.note: Repo is ~110 MB. If pip refuses (macOS 'externally-managed'), create a venv in ~/ppt-master first.

items.name: Marketing Skills
items.what: 52 marketing skills: copywriting, SEO audit, CRO, pricing, email sequences, ads.
items.alt: Pick a few: npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills --skill page-cro copywriting
items.use: Start with the product-marketing-context skill.
items.note: ~15.7k tokens per session for all 52. Installing only the skills you need is much lighter.

items.name: Skills by Anthropic
items.what: Official skills: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, skill-creator, frontend-design, MCP builder.
items.use: Automatic when you ask for a .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf.
items.note: The Claude app already has these built in; this is for Claude Code.

items.name: OpenMontage
items.what: Agentic video studio: research, script, assets, edit and render with 12 pipelines.
items.use: Open Claude Code in ~/OpenMontage and describe the video.
items.tested: make install + preflight OK (local FFmpeg tools ready)
items.note: AGPL-3.0. Generation providers (Veo, Kling, ElevenLabs...) need your own API keys; stock/archive and FFmpeg paths are free.

items.name: Humanizer
items.what: Removes AI-writing tells (based on Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing) with a second audit pass.
items.alt: git clone https://github.com/blader/humanizer.git ~/.claude/skills/humanizer
items.use: /humanizer <paste text>

items.name: HyperFrames
items.what: HeyGen's HTML-to-video renderer with agent skills for captions, transitions, website-to-video.
items.alt: npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes
items.use: /hyperframes 'Make a 10-second product intro.'
items.tested: Installed + validated; doctor needs headless Chrome (browser ensure)

items.name: I Have ADHD
items.what: Ten rules: answer first, numbered steps, max 5 items, no preamble or recap.
items.use: /i-have-adhd once per session; 'stop adhd mode' to turn off.

items.name: Snowflake AI Kit (Cortex Code)
items.what: Official Snowflake plugin: detects Snowflake prompts in Claude Code and routes them to Cortex Code's 55+ Snowflake skills (SQL, dynamic tables, governance, cost).
items.alt: Also in Anthropic's directory: claude plugin install snowflake-cortex-code@claude-plugins-official
items.use: Ask 'show my warehouses and their credit use this week', or $cortex-run <task>.
items.note: Needs the Cortex Code CLI and a Snowflake connection in ~/.snowflake/connections.toml. Its migration agent (in Cortex Code: /migrate) covers Oracle sources and converts Informatica jobs to dbt; Oracle code extraction is marked 'planned' by Snowflake.

items.name: dbt Agent Skills
items.what: dbt Labs' official skills: build models, unit tests, semantic layer, troubleshoot job failures, migrate projects across platforms.
items.alt: npx skills add dbt-labs/dbt-agent-skills
items.use: Automatic on dbt work; try 'why did last night's job fail?'
items.note: dbt-migration includes migrating-dbt-project-across-platforms, useful when moving warehouse SQL to Snowflake.

items.name: dbt MCP server
items.what: Official MCP server: lets Claude run dbt commands, read lineage and model metadata, and query the semantic layer.
items.alt: Register with Claude Code: claude mcp add dbt -- dbt-mcp  (set DBT_PROJECT_DIR and DBT_PATH first)
items.use: claude mcp add dbt -- dbt-mcp, then ask about a model's upstream sources.

items.name: Astronomer Airflow agents
items.what: Airflow MCP server plus skills for authoring, testing and debugging DAGs, lineage tracing and Airflow 2→3 migration. Works with open-source Airflow.
items.alt: npx skills add astronomer/agents --skill '*'
items.use: Set AIRFLOW_API_URL to your Airflow, then 'why did dag X fail last night?'

items.name: Snowflake cost monitoring (dbt)
items.what: dbt package that models Snowflake query cost, warehouse credits and storage, so you can chart spend by team, model and user.
items.alt: Run inside your dbt project (Snowflake adapter). Then: dbt build --select dbt_snowflake_monitoring
items.use: Point a dashboard at the daily_spend and query_history_enriched models.
items.note: Needs a dbt project on Snowflake with a role that can read SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.

ci.skip: needs a dbt project connected to Snowflake; repo and releases are still checked daily

items.name: Elementary (data observability)
items.what: dbt-native data observability: test results, anomaly detection, freshness and lineage in one report, with Slack/Teams alerts.
items.alt: Add the elementary dbt package to packages.yml, dbt run --select elementary, then edr report
items.use: edr report  (opens an HTML report of tests, anomalies and lineage)

items.name: Great Expectations
items.what: Data quality checks as code (expectations) with readable validation reports; runs against Snowflake, Oracle, Spark, pandas.
items.use: Ask Claude to draft expectations for a table from its profile.
items.note: Soda Core is an alternative but uses the Elastic License, which some firms restrict.

items.name: Agent Toolkit for AWS
items.what: AWS's official Claude Code plugins: aws-core (CDK, serverless, observability, billing) and aws-data-analytics (S3 Tables, Glue, Athena, ETL).
items.alt: Also in Anthropic's directory: claude plugin install aws-core@claude-plugins-official
items.use: 'Design a Glue job that lands S3 files into Snowflake' or 'why did this Lambda time out?'
items.note: Uses your AWS credentials; start with a read-only role.

items.name: AWS MCP servers (data & ops)
items.what: AWS Labs MCP servers. Installed here: data processing (Glue, EMR, Athena), CloudWatch logs and metrics, billing and cost, and AWS docs search.
items.alt: Register one: claude mcp add aws-cloudwatch -- awslabs.cloudwatch-mcp-server  (AWS_PROFILE and AWS_REGION set)
items.use: 'Summarize CloudWatch errors for the ingest Lambda in the last 24h.'
items.note: The repo has 60+ servers (Redshift, DynamoDB, Step Functions, IaC...). Read-only IAM first.

items.name: Oracle SQLcl MCP server
items.what: Oracle's official MCP: SQLcl has a built-in MCP server (sql -mcp) that lets Claude run SQL and PL/SQL on your saved Oracle connections. oracle/mcp holds Oracle's other (mostly OCI) servers.
items.alt: Then: claude mcp add oracle -- ~/sqlcl/bin/sql -mcp   (save a connection first with: sql /nolog, then conn -save name -savepwd user@host:port/service)
items.use: 'Explain what PKG_DAILY_LOAD.run does and which tables it writes.'
items.note: Needs Java 17+. Point it at a read-only schema or a dev copy, never production.

items.name: SQLGlot
items.what: SQL parser and transpiler for 30+ dialects. Translates Oracle SQL to Snowflake and gives Claude an exact AST to check rewrites against.
items.verify: python3 -c "import sqlglot; print(sqlglot.transpile('SELECT NVL(a, 0), SYSDATE FROM dual', read='oracle', write='snowflake')[0])"
items.use: python3 -c "import sqlglot; print(sqlglot.transpile(open('q.sql').read(), read='oracle', write='snowflake', pretty=True)[0])"
items.note: Handles SQL, not PL/SQL procedural code; pair it with Claude for packages and procedures.

items.name: SQLFluff
items.what: SQL linter and formatter with Snowflake, Oracle and dbt-templated dialects. Enforces a team style on every pull request.
install: pipx install sqlfluff || python3 -m pip install --user sqlfluff
items.use: sqlfluff lint models/ --dialect snowflake ; sqlfluff fix to auto-format

items.name: Informatica for Claude (IDMC)
items.what: Informatica's official plugin: search the Informatica cloud data catalog (CDGC) for tables, columns, glossary terms and policies from Claude.
items.use: 'Which catalog assets hold customer email, and who owns them?'
items.note: For Informatica's cloud (IDMC). For PowerCenter-to-Snowflake conversion, Snowflake's free SnowConvert AI and Cortex Code's /migrate agent are the tools to evaluate.

items.name: Anthropic knowledge-work plugins
items.what: Anthropic's role plugins. Engineering: standup, code review, incident response, tech debt, system design. Data: SQL, viz, validation. Operations: runbooks, change requests, status reports, risk.
items.alt: Also: productivity@knowledge-work-plugins (tasks and memory). Available in the Claude app too.
items.use: /engineering:standup, /engineering:incident-response, /operations:status-report

items.name: Jira & Confluence MCP (Data Center)
items.what: Open-source MCP server for Jira and Confluence that supports Server/Data Center with a personal access token, as well as Cloud.
items.alt: claude mcp add atlassian -e CONFLUENCE_URL=https://wiki.example.com -e CONFLUENCE_PERSONAL_TOKEN=... -e JIRA_URL=https://jira.example.com -e JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN=... -- mcp-atlassian
items.use: 'List my team's open P1 and P2 tickets older than 5 days and draft the standup summary.'
items.note: Atlassian's official MCP server (atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server) only works with Atlassian Cloud. Use --read-only mode until approved for writes.

items.name: Apache DevLake (DORA dashboards)
items.what: Engineering-metrics platform: pulls Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jenkins, Azure DevOps and SonarQube into ready Grafana dashboards for DORA, sprint flow and code review.
install: mkdir -p ~/devlake && cd ~/devlake && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/apache/devlake/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/apache/devlake/releases/latest/download/env.example && mv env.example .env
cd ~/devlake && echo "ENCRYPTION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 2000 | tr -dc A-Z | fold -w 128 | head -n 1)" >> .env && docker compose up -d
items.alt: Config UI http://localhost:4000, dashboards http://localhost:3002 (admin/admin; change it).
items.verify: cd ~/devlake && docker compose ps --status running | grep -q devlake
items.use: Connect Jira + your Git host in the config UI, then open 'DORA' and 'Jira' dashboards.
items.note: Apache-2.0. Keep ENCRYPTION_SECRET safe; it encrypts the stored tokens.

install: mkdir -p ~/devlake && cd ~/devlake && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/apache/devlake/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml && curl -fsSLO https://github.com/apache/devlake/releases/latest/download/env.example && mv env.example .env && echo ENCRYPTION_SECRET=CITEST >> .env
cd ~/devlake && docker compose config -q && docker compose pull -q
ci.verify: cd ~/devlake && docker compose config --services | grep -q devlake

items.name: Middleware (DORA metrics)
items.what: Lightweight open-source DORA dashboard: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and MTTR from GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
items.alt: Open http://localhost:3333 and connect your Git host.
items.verify: docker ps --filter name=middleware --filter status=running | grep -q middleware
items.use: Review lead time and change failure rate per team every sprint.
items.note: Simpler than DevLake but Git-only (no Jira).

items.name: Claude Code ROI monitoring
items.what: Anthropic's guide and stack for measuring your team's Claude Code usage: OpenTelemetry + Prometheus + Grafana for cost, tokens, sessions, PRs and adoption by developer.
items.alt: Then set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and the OTEL_* variables from claude_code_roi_full.md on each developer machine.
items.use: Share the weekly report built from report-generation-prompt.md.
items.note: Telemetry includes per-user activity: agree on what's collected with your team and firm first.

install: cd ~/claude-code-monitoring-guide && docker compose config -q && docker compose pull -q

items.name: ccusage
items.what: Reads local Claude Code logs and reports tokens and cost by day, session and model. Handy for leads tracking their own and the team's spend.
items.alt: Without installing: npx ccusage@latest daily
items.use: ccusage daily ; ccusage monthly

items.name: Grafana OTel LGTM (all-in-one)
items.what: One container with an OpenTelemetry collector, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope and Grafana: traces, metrics and logs for any app in minutes.
items.alt: Grafana at http://localhost:3000 (admin/admin). Send OTLP to localhost:4317 (gRPC) or 4318 (HTTP).
items.verify: docker ps --filter name=lgtm --filter status=running | grep -q lgtm
items.use: Instrument one service with OpenTelemetry and build its RED dashboard.
items.note: For trials and dev. Production Grafana stacks are usually run by a platform team (Grafana is AGPL-3.0).

items.name: Grafana MCP server
items.what: Official MCP server: Claude searches dashboards, runs PromQL and LogQL, reads alerts and incidents in your Grafana.
items.alt: claude mcp add grafana -e GRAFANA_URL=https://grafana.example.com -e GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=... -- mcp-grafana
items.use: 'What changed on the payments dashboard in the hour before the 2am alert?'
items.note: Use a Viewer-role service account token.

items.name: Keep (alert hub & AIOps)
items.what: Open-source alert management: pulls alerts from Splunk, Dynatrace, Datadog, Prometheus, PagerDuty and 100+ tools into one deduplicated, correlated queue with workflows. Built for L2/L3.
items.alt: UI at http://localhost:3000 (no-auth mode in the default compose file; switch to docker-compose-with-auth.yml for shared use).
items.verify: cd ~/keep && docker compose ps --status running | grep -q keep
items.use: Connect two alert sources, then build a correlation rule for one noisy service.
items.note: MIT.

install: cd ~/keep && docker compose config -q && docker compose pull -q
ci.verify: cd ~/keep && docker compose config --services | grep -q keep-frontend

items.name: HolmesGPT (AI SRE agent)
items.what: CNCF's open-source SRE agent: investigates alerts and incidents across Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Kubernetes, databases and more, and writes root-cause findings back to PagerDuty or Jira.
install: pipx install holmesgpt || python3 -m pip install --user holmesgpt
items.alt: brew tap robusta-dev/homebrew-holmesgpt && brew install holmesgpt
items.use: Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then: holmes ask 'why is the orders API p99 latency up since 09:00?' --model anthropic/<model>
items.note: Point it at read-only data sources; it runs the queries it decides on.

items.name: Uptime Kuma (status pages)
items.what: Self-hosted uptime monitor with public or internal status pages: HTTP, TCP, DNS, database and keyword checks, with Teams, Slack and email alerts.
items.alt: Open http://localhost:3001
items.verify: docker ps --filter name=uptime-kuma --filter status=running | grep -q uptime-kuma
items.use: Give leadership one status page for the services your team owns.
items.note: MIT.

items.name: Dynatrace for AI (plugin + MCP)
items.what: Dynatrace's official Claude Code plugin: skills plus the Dynatrace MCP server to query problems, logs, metrics and traces with DQL, and look up vulnerabilities and service ownership.
items.alt: Remote (no local install): claude mcp add --transport http dynatrace https://<env>.apps.dynatrace.com/platform-reserved/mcp-gateway/v0.1/servers/dynatrace-mcp/mcp  · CLI: brew install dynatrace-oss/tap/dtctl
items.use: export DT_ENVIRONMENT=https://<env>.apps.dynatrace.com DT_PLATFORM_TOKEN=..., start Claude Code, then 'list open problems affecting the trade-capture service'.
items.note: Replaces dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-mcp, archived after v2.1.2. One of the heavier plugins (skills plus the full MCP tool list). Grail queries can incur cost; scope the platform token to read-only.

items.name: PagerDuty MCP server (hosted)
items.what: PagerDuty's official hosted MCP server: incidents, on-call schedules, escalation policies and services from Claude, signed in with OAuth.
install: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http pagerduty https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp
items.alt: The old local server (uvx pagerduty-mcp) still works but no longer gets updates.
items.use: Run /mcp in Claude Code to sign in, then 'who is on call for data-platform tonight, and what fired in the last 7 days?'
items.note: PagerDuty moved development to this hosted server and archived the local repo, which is tracked here for notices.

items.name: Datadog app investigator
items.what: Datadog's official plugin (OAuth login, read-only MCP tools) plus this kit's investigator skill: one report per service with error patterns, slow and failing endpoints, alerting monitors, SLOs, deploys, incidents and next steps.
items.alt: No MCP allowed? The skill's scripts/dd_collect.py does the same with read-only API and application keys from your shell (DD_SITE, DD_API_KEY, DD_APPLICATION_KEY).
items.verify: claude plugin list | grep -q 'top30-ops@top30ongithub' && claude plugin list | grep -q 'datadog@knowledge-work-plugins'
items.use: Run /ddsetup once (pick your Datadog site, sign in in the browser), then: 'investigate orders-api in prod for the last hour'.
items.note: Read-only: the skill uses only Datadog's read tools and masks emails, card numbers and tokens from log lines. Use a Datadog role with read access to the services you support.

items.alt: Full CLI and wizard: npx ruflo@latest init wizard
items.note: Large and fast-moving. Its other plugins range from security audits to trading bots; add them one at a time.
items.name: Ruflo (agent swarms)
items.what: Runs coordinated agent swarms across Claude Code and Codex with shared vector memory, workflows and an MCP server. 47 plugins; this installs only the core.
items.use: Ask for a multi-agent plan on a large change; add ruflo-rag-memory or ruflo-adr only if you need them.

items.alt: Others worth a look: observability-monitoring, database-cloud-optimization, comprehensive-review
items.note: Plugins are small and separate by design: install only the ones for your work.
items.name: wshobson agents (plugin packs)
items.what: 94 focused plugins (202 agents, 185 skills). Installed here: data-engineering (ETL, warehouse design), incident-response and team-collaboration (standups, issue workflows).
items.use: Ask for a warehouse design review, or run the incident-response triage workflow.

items.alt: npx skills add OthmanAdi/planning-with-files --skill planning-with-files -g
items.note: Built for long tasks that survive /clear. On short single-session coding tasks an independent placebo test (skill-placebo) found a lower pass rate (80% vs 100% for a placebo), so use it for multi-day work, not everything.
items.name: planning-with-files
items.what: Keeps the plan, findings and progress in markdown files on disk, so long tasks survive /clear, compaction and crashes.
items.use: Start a multi-day migration with it; the plan files become the hand-off between sessions.

items.alt: macOS: brew install rtk-ai/tap/rtk-oss && rtk init -g
items.note: Use the OSS edition (Apache-2.0); the default download adds a BUSL-1.1 engine. rtk init -g adds a hook and edits your global CLAUDE.md. rtk notes that smaller bash output is not the same as an equally smaller bill.
items.name: rtk (OSS edition)
items.what: Rust CLI proxy that compresses common dev command output (git, tests, builds, logs) before the agent reads it; the project reports 60-90% smaller bash output.
items.use: rtk gain  (shows tokens saved)

install: RTK_VERSION=$(git ls-remote --tags --refs https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk.git | grep -oE 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1) && curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | RTK_EDITION=oss RTK_VERSION=$RTK_VERSION sh

items.alt: MCP only: claude mcp add context-mode -- npx -y context-mode
items.note: Elastic License 2.0, not open source: check with your firm before work use.
items.name: context-mode
items.what: Runs tool output in a sandbox and returns only what matters to the model; the project reports 315 KB of raw output reduced to 5.4 KB.
items.use: Works automatically on large tool outputs; /context-mode:stats shows savings.

items.note: Rendering needs Node and Chromium (Remotion).
items.name: video-shotcraft
items.what: Turns your real web pages into a cinematic product video in Remotion, with cuts synced to the music's beat.
items.use: 'Make a 30-second product video from https://my-app.example.com'

items.alt: Windows and Linux: download from https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/releases
items.note: Stores provider API keys locally; at work, use only the providers your firm approves.
items.name: CC Switch (desktop)
items.what: Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) to switch Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI between providers in one click and manage MCP servers, skills and prompts in one place.
items.use: Keep personal and work provider settings apart.

ci.skip: desktop app; releases and upstream are still checked daily

items.alt: Also: pm-product-discovery, pm-product-strategy, pm-data-analytics
items.name: pm-skills
items.what: 69 product-management skills and 42 chained workflows. Installed here: pm-execution (PRDs, OKRs, roadmaps, sprint plans, pre-mortems, stakeholder maps).
items.use: 'Draft a one-page PRD and a pre-mortem for the Snowflake cost dashboard.'

items.alt: Also relevant: data-quality-auditor, chief-data-officer-advisor, executive-mentor
items.note: 104 plugins: pick a few, each one adds to every session.
items.name: claude-skills (380+ skills)
items.what: Large skill library across engineering, product, compliance and leadership. Installed here: engineering-skills, vpe-advisor (DORA and cycle-time analysis) and slo-architect.
items.use: 'Analyze our last quarter's delivery: DORA metrics and where cycle time goes.'

items.alt: No install: the Google Sheets version linked from the README. AWS shops: the AmazonBedrock folder runs the same course on Bedrock (boto3).
items.note: The notebooks call Claude 3 Haiku and Sonnet, which Anthropic retired (Haiku 3 on April 20, 2026), so the install switches them to Claude Haiku 4.5. Newer models (4.6+) reject the temperature and prefill settings the lessons use. No licence file upstream: fine to learn from, not to redistribute.
items.name: Prompt engineering tutorial
items.what: Anthropic's 9-chapter interactive course in Jupyter notebooks: prompt structure, clarity, roles, separating data from instructions, output formatting, step-by-step thinking, examples, avoiding hallucinations, complex prompts (incl. financial services). Appendix: chaining, tool use, retrieval.
install: uv tool install jupyterlab --with anthropic --with pip
items.use: cd ~/claude-learn/prompt-eng-interactive-tutorial/'Anthropic 1P' && jupyter-lab   then open 00_Tutorial_How-To and paste a Console API key

items.note: Each app has its own dependencies (Node, Python, Docker for computer use). Starting points, not production code.
items.name: Claude quickstarts
items.what: 17 deployable starter apps on the Claude API: customer support agent, financial data analyst, computer and browser use, an autonomous coding agent on the Agent SDK, and Managed Agents apps (Slack and Linear bots, a daily Slack/GitHub brief, an SEC-filings knowledge wiki, Sentry triage).
items.use: Start with financial-data-analyst or managed-agents/daily-brief; each folder's README has its setup. Needs an API key.

items.alt: Any Python 3.10+ environment: pip install claude-agent-sdk. TypeScript: npm install @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
items.note: Uses whatever Claude Code auth the machine has: your login, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 with AWS credentials. Governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms.
items.name: Claude Agent SDK (Python)
items.what: The Claude Code agent loop as a Python library: your own tools (in-process MCP), hooks that allow or deny each action, subagents, budgets. Bundles the Claude Code CLI. This kit includes a working example, examples/sql-review-agent: a read-only Snowflake SQL reviewer.
items.use: From this kit's folder: ~/claude-learn/agent-venv/bin/python examples/sql-review-agent/agent.py examples/sql-review-agent/sample

items.alt: brew install --cask claude-code  ·  Windows: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex  ·  winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode (npm install is deprecated)
items.note: The GitHub repo holds docs, issues and the changelog; the source isn't open (Anthropic's Commercial Terms). Official plugins live in anthropics/claude-plugins-official.
items.name: Claude Code (the CLI)
items.what: The agent in your terminal: reads the codebase, edits files, runs commands, handles git. Every plugin in this kit runs inside it.
items.use: cd your-repo && claude

items.alt: Inside a repo you admin: run claude, then /install-github-app (direct Anthropic API only)
items.note: Runs on your own runners; code goes to the model provider you choose (Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry). Repo admin rights needed. At work, use your firm's approved provider and GitHub App.
items.name: Claude Code Action (GitHub)
items.what: Claude Code in GitHub Actions: tag @claude on a PR or issue to get an answer, a review or a pushed fix; or run it on every PR. Installs two ready workflows from this kit: @claude mentions (Anthropic API) and a Snowflake SQL review on Amazon Bedrock via OIDC.
install: for f in claude.yml sql-review-bedrock.yml sql_checks.py; do curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/venkatesanps/top30ongithub/main/templates/claude-code-action/$f -o ~/claude-learn/claude-code-action/$f; done
items.use: Copy a workflow into your repo's .github/workflows/; each file's header lists the secrets it needs.

items.alt: npx skills add kepano/obsidian-skills --skill defuddle --skill json-canvas --skill obsidian-markdown -g -a claude-code -y
items.note: defuddle runs the Defuddle CLI (npm install -g defuddle). The plugin also brings obsidian-bases and obsidian-cli; the cli skill needs Obsidian's desktop CLI.
items.name: Obsidian Skills
items.what: Skills from Obsidian's CEO: defuddle turns a web page into clean markdown (fewer tokens than a raw fetch), json-canvas draws mind maps as Obsidian canvases, obsidian-markdown writes notes with wikilinks, callouts and properties.
items.use: 'Save this article as an Obsidian note with tags: <url>', or 'map this design doc as a canvas'.

items.note: Works by driving a real Chrome signed in to your Google account, and sets up its own Python environment on first use. Personal notebooks only: don't point it at work documents or a work account.
items.name: NotebookLM skill
items.what: Asks your Google NotebookLM notebooks questions from Claude Code and brings back answers grounded in, and cited to, the documents you uploaded there.
items.use: 'Ask my Snowflake-docs notebook how dynamic tables refresh.' The first run opens a browser so you can sign in to Google.

items.alt: claude plugin marketplace add huggingface/skills && claude plugin install hf-cli@huggingface-skills
items.note: About 25 more skills in the repo (datasets, training, Spaces, SageMaker deployment). Its plugin marketplace only ships the hf-cli skill, so this installs the three by name.
items.name: Hugging Face skills
items.what: Hugging Face's own skills. Installed here: huggingface-papers (find and read AI papers), huggingface-gradio (quick demo apps) and huggingface-local-models (pick and run open models on your machine).
install: npx -y skills add huggingface/skills --skill huggingface-papers --skill huggingface-gradio --skill huggingface-local-models -g -a claude-code -y
items.use: 'Find this month's papers on text-to-SQL and summarize the two most cited.'

items.note: Written for the n8n-mcp server (czlonkowski/n8n-mcp), which lets Claude read and validate workflows on your n8n instance. The plugin adds hooks that check workflow edits.
items.name: n8n skills
items.what: 15 skills for building n8n workflows: expression syntax, node configuration, workflow patterns, reading validation errors, code nodes, error handling and sub-workflows.
items.use: Paste a failing workflow's error: 'why does this {{ $json.date }} expression fail in the Set node?'

items.note: The repo has no license file, so this kit installs from upstream but doesn't repackage it as Claude app zips. Deploying needs a Vercel account.
items.name: Vercel agent skills
items.what: Vercel's skills. Installed here: deploy-to-vercel (deploy and get a preview link), react-best-practices (performance rules for React and Next.js) and web-design-guidelines (audits UI code for accessibility and UX problems).
install: npx -y skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill deploy-to-vercel --skill vercel-react-best-practices --skill web-design-guidelines -g -a claude-code -y
items.use: 'Review my dashboard's components against the web design guidelines', then 'deploy a preview'.

items.note: CC BY-SA 4.0. The same marketplace has 70+ security skills (CodeQL, fuzzing, differential review) worth a look for code review.
items.name: Trail of Bits skills
items.what: Security firm Trail of Bits' skills. Installed here: modern-python, which sets up and keeps Python projects on uv, ruff and current tooling instead of pip and setup.py.
items.use: 'Convert my refiner scripts repo to uv with ruff and a lockfile.'

items.note: Reference material more than a workflow: useful while designing an agent, then disable it.
items.name: Context engineering skills
items.what: How context works and how to manage it when building agents: context-fundamentals, degradation, compression, tool design, memory and multi-agent patterns.
items.use: 'Why does my agent forget the schema after 40 turns, and what should go in its context instead?'

items.alt: Browse and copy at https://easyui.site/components; llms.txt at https://easyui.site/llms.txt
items.note: MIT. Copy-paste source, so audit what you add: this kit's registry_kit.py audit (a heuristic check) found 71 of 132 components animating with no reduced-motion handling, and command-menu and spotlight-search import a site-only file the registry doesn't ship, so they don't compile after install. The top30-ui plugin builds your own library the same way.
items.name: EasyUI
items.what: 132 animated React components (Tailwind, Framer Motion, TypeScript) published as a shadcn GitHub registry: magnetic buttons, docks, morphing dialogs, charts, OTP and command menus.
items.use: In a React + Tailwind project with shadcn set up: npx shadcn@latest add Surajmaurya1/easyui/<name>.

items.alt: npx skills add jakubkrehel/skills -g -a claude-code -y
items.note: MIT. EasyUI's repo uses these (its skills-lock.json). explain-interface pairs with this kit's ui-reverse-engineer agent; interface-review fits PR checks.
items.name: Interfaces skills
items.what: 14 interface skills by Jakub Krehel: better-ui, better-accessibility, better-typography, better-colors, better-layout, better-writing, interface-review for a branch or PR, explain-interface (how a site or animation was built, from a URL or screenshot), state-machine and variant.
items.use: 'Review this branch with interface-review', or 'explain-interface: how is the hover effect on <url> built?'

items.alt: Busabase Cloud: claude plugin marketplace add busabase/skills && claude plugin install busabase@busabase (hosted MCP, browser sign-in). Self-host: docker run -p 15419:15419 -v ~/.busabase/data:/data busabase/busabase
items.note: MIT, runs locally (embedded Postgres, data in ~/.busabase) or self-hosted in Docker. Agent writes are change requests with an author, diff and history; a credential limited to proposing means edits wait for a person, the 'closed lane' from playbooks/loops-and-graphs.md. Claude-Mem (15) remembers one person's sessions; Busabase is a shared record for many agents and people. Young project: get approval before putting work data in it.
items.name: Busabase
items.what: A shared, versioned workspace for agents and people: typed tables, docs, skills, playbooks and small apps that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and n8n read and write through a skill, MCP, OpenAPI or a CLI, so the next session starts from what the last one recorded.
items.use: Start a workspace with `npx -y busabase@latest server`, then tell Claude: 'Read and follow http://localhost:15419/SETUP_SKILL.md'. Later: 'What changed on this project this week?'

install: setsid npx -y busabase@latest server > /tmp/busabase.log 2>&1 & pg=$!; for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sf http://localhost:15419/SETUP_SKILL.md > /tmp/busabase-setup.md && break; sleep 3; done; kill -- -$pg 2>/dev/null || true; grep -q '^name: busabase' /tmp/busabase-setup.md

open20.label: 20 to open first
advice: Start with 3, not 20: one for memory, one for tokens, one for your actual job.
Run the same task before and after. Keep only what makes the result better or cheaper.
Every plugin you add loads into context, so more isn't free.
open20.heading: Before you open all 20
open20.source: From the post "20 GitHub projects you should open first".

anthropic6.label: Anthropic's 6 to build with
anthropic6.heading: Build one agent, not six demos
anthropic6.source: From the post on Anthropic's six GitHub repos to build with.
advice: Learn the prompt basics first (67): a couple of evenings, and every agent after it is cheaper and more reliable.
Build one agent for a real, repetitive task on your team. examples/sql-review-agent is a working start: a custom tool, a read-only guard and a budget cap.
Put it where the team already works: claude-code-action runs it on every pull request (a Bedrock version is included).
Measure it like any tool: same task before and after, keep it only if it's better or cheaper.

skills27.label: 27 skills, one at a time
skills27.heading: Don't install all 27 tonight
skills27.source: From the post listing 27 skills in five folders (notes, writing, marketing, automation, build & ship).
advice: Pick the folder closest to your daily work and add one skill from it.
Use it on real tasks for a week. Keep it if it saved time, then add the next one.
Three skills you use every day beat 27 you never open. The kit's skill-trial skill (top30-coach) keeps score for you.
